title: TMCP CapabilityReport
description: Response contract for the can_do tool. Returns a structured report of which capabilities are feasible (candidates), which matched semantically but cannot execute (blocked), surrounding context, and query metadata. Orchestrators must check valid_until on each candidate before executing a do_* derived from this report.

query_id.description: UUIDv4 identifying this specific can_do query. Used for deduplication in distributed deployments and for correlating the plan step with subsequent do_* calls in audit logs.

feasible.description: true if and only if at least one candidate has permission: 'allowed'. false means no immediately executable path exists — inspect blocked[] to determine recoverability.

candidates.description: Tools that semantically match the intent and are currently executable. Ordered by confidence descending. May be empty.

capability.description: Full tool name of the matching capability. Example: 'do_transfer_stock', 'do_set_fan_speed'.

source.description: Identifier of the server or node exposing this capability. Example: 'inventory-server', 'node_hvac_zone3_007'.

confidence.description: Semantic match strength between the intent query and this capability. 1.0 = exact match. Below 0.7: orchestrator SHOULD escalate to human review or request clarification before executing do_*.

permission.description: Current execution permission for this candidate. Only 'allowed' permits autonomous do_* execution. 'requires_human_approval' permits execution only after explicit human confirmation. All other values belong in blocked[].

valid_until.description: ISO 8601 datetime after which this candidate's permission snapshot is no longer valid. Orchestrator MUST re-call can_do if now() >= valid_until before executing do_*. A missing valid_until MUST be treated as zero validity window.

current_state.description: Current observed value of the capability's target, if available. Saves a read_* round-trip for simple decision logic.

constraints.description: Value bounds for this capability. Use to validate the intended value before executing do_*.

enum_values.description: Valid discrete values for enum-typed capabilities.

side_effects.description: Declared side effects this capability will produce upon execution. Exposed pre-execution so the orchestrator can reason about downstream impact before committing.

estimated_latency_ms.description: Estimated round-trip latency in milliseconds for the do_* call. Optional. Used by orchestrators optimizing parallel execution plans.

blocked.description: Tools that matched the intent semantically but cannot execute in the current state. Always include these — they tell the orchestrator why options are unavailable and whether the situation is recoverable.

capability.description: Full tool name of the blocked capability.

source.description: Identifier of the server or node exposing this capability.

permission.description: Reason category for the block. Used by the orchestrator to determine recoverability without parsing the reason string.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation of why this capability is blocked. Example: 'Transfer limit of 10/hour exceeded', 'Device offline since 14:30 UTC', 'Cooldown active for 28 more seconds'.

details.description: Optional machine-parseable additional detail. Examples: 'Window resets at 2026-04-30T17:00:00Z', 'last_seen: 4 minutes ago', 'required_role: supervisor'.

context.description: Surrounding state to inform agent decisions before executing do_*.

related_reads.description: List of read_* tool names the orchestrator MAY call for additional context. These are safe to fan out in parallel before the do_* step.

current_observations.description: Inline observations of related state, keyed by read_* tool name or semantic label. Provided opportunistically to reduce round-trips.

metadata.description: Diagnostics and observability for this can_do query.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 datetime when the CapabilityReport was generated.

total_latency_ms.description: Total wall-clock time in milliseconds from query receipt to response.
